swiftui_behaviors.onAppear_in_ScrollView: All child views inside a ScrollView fire .onAppear simultaneously when the ScrollView first renders, NOT when each child scrolls into view. This means if 4 sections each trigger an action in .onAppear, all 4 actions execute at the same time on first render.
swiftui_behaviors.alert_collision: If multiple .alert(isPresented:) modifiers are attached to the same view and multiple bindings are set to true in the same frame (or within a short window), only the LAST one set actually displays. Earlier alerts are silently swallowed by SwiftUI. This is a known SwiftUI limitation.
swiftui_behaviors.state_vs_appstorage: @State resets when the view is recreated (e.g., navigating away and back). @AppStorage persists to UserDefaults and survives view recreation. Use @AppStorage for settings that should persist across sessions, @State for ephemeral UI state.
swiftui_behaviors.binding_propagation: @Binding changes in child views immediately propagate to the parent. If a parent has .alert(isPresented: $binding) and a child sets binding = true in .onAppear, the alert fires on the parent view. Combined with onAppear_in_ScrollView, this creates race conditions when multiple children set different bindings.
swiftui_behaviors.environmentobject_crash: If a view uses @EnvironmentObject but the object is not provided by an ancestor via .environmentObject(), the app crashes at runtime with no compile-time warning. This is a common source of crashes when views are presented in sheets or navigation destinations without re-injecting environment objects.
swiftui_behaviors.geometryreader_sizing: GeometryReader proposes the full available size to its child, but the child's frame determines the GeometryReader's own size. Wrapping content in GeometryReader can cause unexpected layout behavior if the content doesn't explicitly set its frame.
swiftui_behaviors.published_existential_limitation: @Published does not work correctly with existential types (any Protocol). The property wrapper cannot detect changes through the existential wrapper. Workaround: use willSet { objectWillChange.send() } instead of @Published for existential-typed properties.
